subject: AcmeHealth private/VPC post-call recap: networking, data residency, next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeHealth private/VPC post-call recap: networking, data residency, next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call so we all have the same view and next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Key pain points you raised
- Strict data residency: PHI must remain in AcmeHealth-controlled VPCs or on-prem.
- Air-gap / limited egress: Security team requires minimal outgoing connections from inference runtime; some environments will be air-gapped.
- Networking constraints: No public IPs on model hosts; inbound through specific bastions / NATs only.
- Audit & key management: Customer-managed KMS and detailed audit logs required for compliance.

Goals we aligned on
- Proof-of-concept private deployment in your staging VPC (non-prod) that demonstrates inference latency SLA and meets network egress constraints.
- Provide a deployment plan that outlines networking requirements, a step-by-step install for air-gapped mode, and KMS integration.
- Deliver SOC2 + customer-facing security checklist and an architecture diagram for your ops/security teams.

Actions / next steps
1) AcmeHealth: Share the VPC CIDR ranges, egress restrictions, and preferred bastion/NAT hostname (Tom to send) — due: Wed 3/10 EOD.
2) Redwood (Camila/Marissa): Provide network requirements doc and private deployment overview; include air-gap checklist and KMS integration notes — due: Fri 3/12. Attachment: redwood_private_overview.pdf.
3) Schedule technical deep dive with your Security and Network engineers to walk through firewall rules, proxy requirements, and the air-gap install flow (30–45m). Proposed times: Tue 3/16 or Wed 3/17 — do these work?
4) Share SOC2 / compliance artifacts and any required attestation forms.

Attachments I mentioned during the call: redwood_private_overview.pdf (private deploy overview), acme_network_requirements.pdf (template for your team to populate).

Thanks — really appreciate the clear constraints. We’ll make the doc as prescriptive as possible so your ops team can validate quickly.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Note: If helpful I can also include an example iptables/proxy config for the air-gapped installer in the next delivery.

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmehealth.com>, IT Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private/VPC post-call recap: networking, data residency, next steps

Camila —

Thanks for the thorough recap. That matches our notes. A couple of clarifications:
- For the POC we can provide a non-prod VPC with a transit gateway and a single NAT bastion. No public IPs on the model hosts is non-negotiable.
- Air-gap mode: our security team wants a signed installer and no outbound connections except to our internal update mirror.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS with a customer-owned CMK; we will need instructions for key rotation and how Redwood will reference the CMK.

I attached our baseline network constraints document — it’s not complete but will give you what to start with. Tom will follow up with the CIDRs and the bastion hostname by EOD tomorrow.

Samantha
Director of IT Architecture | AcmeHealth
samantha.lee@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Attachment: acme_network_requirements.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private/VPC post-call recap: networking, data residency, next steps

Samantha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachment. We’ll review the network constraints doc and incorporate the specifics into the POC plan. A few notes on our side:
- Air-gapped installer: we support an offline install that runs from a signed tarball. We’ll include an example update-mirror config so your ops team can host approved package artifacts internally.
- KMS: we support customer-owned AWS CMKs. We’ll document the minimal IAM permissions required and a recommended rotation process.
- No-public-IP installs: supported; we’ll provide the exact ports and IPs that need to be allowed on your bastion and LB.

Proposed mutual action plan (summary)
- 3/10: AcmeHealth provides CIDRs + bastion hostname (Tom).
- 3/12: Redwood delivers detailed network & air-gap deployment doc + SOC2 excerpt and audit checklist (Camila/Marissa).
- 3/16–3/17: Technical deep dive with Security & Network (30–45m).
- 3/26: Initial POC deploy in non-prod VPC.

I’ll attach the redwood_private_overview.pdf to the same HubSpot deal card and share the DocuSign link for our standard POC SOW (low-effort, covers responsibilities and timelines). DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/s/ABCDEF1234567890

If that timeline looks good I’ll lock in a time for the deep dive.

Thanks,
Camila

---
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private/VPC post-call recap: networking, data residency, next steps

Looping in our security lead (Laura) to cover the SOC2 artifacts and to join the technical deep dive. Laura — can you confirm availability on 3/16 (10–11am PT) or 3/17 (1–2pm PT)?

Camila — I’ll draft the POC SOW and put the redwood_private_overview.pdf and the socket-level port list into the HubSpot deal. Planning to include an example iptables snippet for the air-gapped installer as you suggested.

Sincerely,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
